arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Stewart cited Defenders of Wildlife to define injury in fact.
He stated injury must be concrete, particularized, and actual or imminent.
Mr. Pincus argued the constitutional minimum is injury in fact.
He noted Congress can elevate de facto injuries to legal status in Lujan.

paragraphs: Spokeo wants the Court to require proof of tangible harm beyond a statutory violation.

Robins argues that Congress can define a statutory violation as a concrete injury.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the minimum injury required to sue in federal court. It determines whether statutory violations alone grant access to the judiciary. The outcome shapes the scope of consumer protection laws. It affects how courts interpret congressional definitions of harm.
